words: The budget is the integer key chain_left: the number of further days one chain may build after the day an invocation builds. It is validated in _event_budget before any client is created or any call is made: it must be an int that is not a bool and lies from 0 to 9, and any other value refuses with SystemExit naming chain_left. An event without the key (the scheduled fire, an empty event, an explicit day event) starts a chain with 9, so one chain builds at most 10 days in all. chain_next self-invokes the next owed day with chain_left one less only while chain_left is above 0 and an owed day exists; a day built at 0 chains nothing and the chain states capped. The cap now holds across the whole chain because the budget travels in each self-invoke payload, where before only the owed list was capped and every hop recomputed that list from the newest landed day. NOT PROVEN: the Lambda runtime and the deployed function, which still holds the earlier code until a later code-update pair ships this handler.
